name: United Nations Blue
lede: United Nations Blue is a vivid, greenish blue taken from the United Nations flag, an institution's color rather than a pigment or dye.

sections.title: A flag's blue
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which gives no date for when the United Nations adopted this exact shade for its emblem and world map [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for the region reads "vivid greenish blue" [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[weezy-blue]], 2.9 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as almost the same [2]. [[carolina-blue]] sits at 4.4, duller, [[blue-jeans]] at 7.2, bluer and lighter, and [[cerulean-sea]] at 7.8, darker [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 61, chroma 43, a bright, strongly saturated blue [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in just 4 of 23,781 paintings (0.02 percent), rarer than 83 percent of the named colors, as photographed [3]. A flag color this recent and this saturated has little reason to turn up in centuries-old paintings, so the scarcity is unsurprising [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
